record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.original_question: If f is a strictly ergodic smooth diffeomorphism of a compact connected manifold M^n, meaning that f is both minimal and uniquely ergodic, must the topological entropy of f be equal to 0?

evidence.quote: 4.10 - Let Mn be compact connected manifold and f a strictly ergodic C∞ -diﬀeomorphism (minimal (i.e. every orbit is dense) and uniquely ergodic). Conjecture. The topological entropy of f equals 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M^n$ be a compact connected smooth manifold of dimension $n$, and let $f: M^n \to M^n$ be a $C^\infty$-diffeomorphism. Recall that $f$ is called:
- minimal if every orbit $\{f^k(x) : k \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ is dense in $M^n$;
- uniquely ergodic if there exists exactly one $f$-invariant Borel probability measure on $M^n$;
- strictly ergodic if it is both minimal and uniquely ergodic.

The topological entropy $h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$ is defined as
$$h_{\mathrm{top}}(f) = \lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n} \log s(n, \varepsilon),$$
where $s(n, \varepsilon)$ denotes the maximal cardinality of an $(n, \varepsilon)$-separated subset of $M^n$ with respect to any fixed Riemannian metric.

Prove or disprove: every strictly ergodic $C^\infty$-diffeomorphism $f$ of a compact connected manifold $M^n$ satisfies $h_{\mathrm{top}}(f) = 0$.
artifact.category_tag: smooth ergodic theory and topological entropy
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that every strictly ergodic smooth diffeomorphism of a compact manifold has zero topological entropy appears to still be open. Known related results include: uniquely ergodic homeomorphisms can have positive topological entropy (Hahn–Katznelson, Rees, Béguin–Crovisier–Le Roux); Herman constructed minimal $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms with positive entropy, but those examples are not uniquely ergodic. A separate conjecture of Herman regarding perturbations of the identity to a positive-entropy area-preserving diffeomorphism was proved by Berger and Turaev (2017–2019), but that is a different statement and does not address the strict ergodicity vs. zero entropy question.

status_evidence.title: On Herman's Positive Entropy Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Berger and Turaev prove a different Herman conjecture concerning perturbations of the identity yielding positive metric entropy.
status_evidence.claim: Resolves a different Herman conjecture, not the strict ergodicity vs. zero entropy one.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress in Dynamics, MSRI Publications Vol. 54 (Open Problems)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including questions on whether smooth uniquely ergodic diffeomorphisms can have positive entropy.
status_evidence.claim: The smooth strictly ergodic vs. zero-entropy question is recorded as open.
